battle.title: Tree Traversal Trek
battle.description: Climb through preorder, inorder and postorder without losing your branch.

questions.text: What does an inorder traversal of a binary search tree produce?
options: Values in the order they were inserted
questions.explanation: Inorder visits left subtree, node, then right subtree, and in a BST everything left is smaller and everything right is larger. Level order and insertion order are different things.
Preorder visits the node first, then the left subtree, then the right: 1, then 2 with its children 4 and 5, then 3. 4 2 5 1 3 is inorder and 4 5 2 3 1 is postorder.
The BST is 5 with left child 3 (children 1 and 4) and right child 8. Postorder visits both subtrees before the node: 1 4 3, then 8, then 5. 1 3 4 5 8 would be inorder.

questions.text: You need to visit the nodes of a tree level by level, all nodes at depth 0, then depth 1, and so on. Which technique fits?
questions.explanation: A queue processes nodes in the order they were discovered, which naturally gives one depth after another. The three depth-first traversals dive down a branch before visiting siblings.
Inserting already sorted values 1,2,3,4 into a BST makes a chain of height 4, while 2,1,3 is balanced with height 2. This shows why an unbalanced BST degrades toward O(n) operations.

coding.title: BST Traversal Report
coding.description: Insert n integers, in the given order, into an initially empty binary search tree (smaller values go left, larger go right, a duplicate of a value already in the tree is ignored). Print four lines: the preorder traversal, the inorder traversal, the postorder traversal (values separated by single spaces) and finally the height of the tree, where a single node has height 1.
coding.outputDescription: Four lines: preorder, inorder, postorder, then the height.

debug.title: Sorted Out of Order
debug.description: The program inserts n distinct integers into a binary search tree and should print them in ascending order using an inorder traversal. The numbers come out in a different order. Input: n, then n integers. Output: the values in ascending order separated by spaces.
hints: Insert 5, 3, 8 and compare what is printed to the sorted list 3 5 8.
The tree is built correctly. Focus on the order of the three statements inside inorder.
Inorder means left subtree, then the node, then right subtree. Where is the node's value being printed?
Recurse on n.l first, then append n.v, then recurse on n.r.
